BRAKE ASSIST 
Brake Assist helps in emergency situations when pressure on the  
brake pedal is insufficient during sudden or ‘panic’ braking.
VSC (Vehicle Stability Control) system  
VSC (Vehicle Stability Control) system helps to prevent wheel slip  
when turning a vehicle or during sudden steering situations.
•  Brake Assist helps to apply full braking force when it detects that the pressure that is applied  
on the brake pedal is insufficient.

The illustration shows what happens to the car after the driver rapidly turns the steering wheel 
in mid-corner. With the aid of VSC, the car maneuvers properly and is able to quickly return 
to its original lane.
Reminder: VSC does not eliminate the danger of accidents. It only assists with vehicle stability.

ai_answer: Brake Assist is an electronic safety feature that steps in when the driver tries to brake suddenly but does not press the pedal hard enough—such as during a panic‑stop. The vehicle’s control computer constantly monitors how quickly and how forcefully the brake pedal is being pressed. If it determines that the driver’s input is fast and hard enough to indicate an emergency, but the actual pedal pressure is still insufficient to achieve maximum braking, the system automatically adds the extra force needed to bring the brakes to full‑bias. In this way, Brake Assist ensures that full braking force is applied even when the driver’s foot pressure alone would be inadequate, helping to shorten stopping distances in emergency situations.
